title: Latency & Billing Triage — Stitch Weeknotes (2026-12-16)
content:
Context:
This week’s hybrid standup focused on a subtle billing/latency coupling surfaced by Finance: a ~14% increase in GPU billing on Hosted API for the streaming chat routes during 2026-12-09 -> 2026-12-15. Backend SRE picked up a matching uptick in average span counts per request on the streaming proxy. We ran a focused triage Wednesday and captured notes here — purpose is to record findings, decisions, and follow-ups for the next sprint.

Attendees:
- Maya Chen (obs lead)
- Arjun Rao (SRE, tracing)
- Priya Kapoor (cost telemetry)
- Diego Morales (runtime infra)
- Claire Nguyen (product, hosted-api, joined 20m)

High-level summary / hypothesis:
- Symptom A: Finance observed +14% GPU billing for hosted streaming endpoints week-over-week.
- Symptom B: End-to-end p50 latency for streaming endpoints rose from ~120ms to ~170ms for token emit.
- Observation: Span counts per request increased by median +35% on the streaming proxy (proxy spans and repeated serialize/deserialize loops).
- Working hypothesis: A recent change in the streaming proxy error-handling path (retry-on-interrupt) created repeated short-lived internal requests that increase KV cache churn and cause additional offload work on the serving runtime, increasing GPU cycles per logical request.

Evidence we collected:
- Trace samples: We pulled 200 high-span traces (OBS-5472) across the time window. Patterns show: repeated IRequest spans with identical trace ids and short gaps (~15–40ms) between them.
- Dashboard deltas: Streaming-route span histogram shows a right-shift in 95th percentile span counts. Per-route cost breakdown dashboard shows increase in per-request GPU-ms correlated with span count.
- Logs: Proxy logs include a new WARN code (RP-204) introduced in commit 8f3b2a5 that correlates with the start of the spike window.
- Runtime metrics: KV cache eviction rate on nv_cache increased 3x during peak windows, and GPU utilization climbed by ~6 p.p. during the same intervals.

Immediate actions taken in the triage:
- Hotfix candidate: revert RP-204 path in the streaming proxy and run canary on 5% traffic. Diego to own (GH PR linked).
- Sampling change: temporarily raise trace_sample_rate for streaming proxy from 1% to 0.5% to reduce ingestion load for the telemetry pipeline while we debug (Arjun).
- Dashboard adjustments: Added a cross-filtered panel in the Cost -> Hosted API view to show per-request GPU-ms vs span count to make correlation visible to Finance (Priya).
- Alert tuning: created short-lived alert OBS-BILL-SHORT to warn on >10% WoW billing change for streaming routes (Maya).

Detailed notes / findings:
- Root-cause suspicion: The retry-on-interrupt code path creates a new internal request without propagating the existing KV cache handle, forcing the runtime to recreate per-request GPU state and re-warm KV cache entries. This multiplies work per logical user request.
- Repro attempt: Diego recreated a local workload with artificially triggered interrupts and reproduced increased GPU-ms / higher span counts. Repro script: telemetry-config/testbeds/repro/retry-loop.sh (branch repro-retry-loop).
- Cost model: Priya estimated the incremental cost at ~9–12% of the observed billing delta once accounting for granularity and burst windows — aligns with Finance’s ballpark numbers after adjusting for sampling.

Decisions made:
- Roll forward plan: Do not roll the proxy revert to 100% until after canary results. If canary reduces span counts and GPU-ms match baseline within 24h we will graduate. Diego to monitor canary and coordinate rollback if adverse.
- Telemetry sampling: Keep lowered sample rate for 48 hours, then re-evaluate after canary results (Arjun + Priya).
- Dashboard permanence: Convert the ad-hoc panel into a permanent per-route cost/trace correlation card if the correlation holds post-fix (Product + Obs).

Action items (owners & ETA):
- Diego Morales: Open PR and deploy canary revert of RP-204 to 5% traffic. Start: 2026-12-16 11:00 PT. ETA: 2026-12-16 14:00 PT. Status: in progress. (GH PR: linked_artifacts above)
- Arjun Rao: Reduce trace sample rate on streaming proxy pipeline; add a temporary filter to drop internal retry traces. ETA: 2026-12-16 EOD. Status: done (temporary).
- Priya Kapoor: Add GPU-ms vs span count correlation card to Hosted API cost dashboard; capture initial snapshot and share with Finance. ETA: 2026-12-17. Status: in progress.
- Maya Chen: Create OBS-BILL-SHORT alert & coordinate with Finance for threshold tuning. ETA: 2026-12-17. Status: done.
- Claire Nguyen: Triage product tolerance — how aggressive can we be with retry changes without user-visible regressions. Provide acceptance criteria. ETA: 2026-12-18. Status: pending.

Open questions / risks:
- Is there a separate user-triggered scenario that produces similar pattern (e.g., client reconnects)? We could be masking a client issue with proxy retries. (Action: add client-side correlation sample).
- Telemetry bias risk: lowering sample rate temporarily may hide low-frequency but high-cost traces. Keep short window and re-run sampling after fix.
- Canary risk: Reverting the path may reduce resilience against transient infra interrupts. Need to confirm product acceptance criteria with Claire before full roll.

Follow-ups for next week (planned sprint items):
- Longer-term fix: ensure KV cache handles are propagated across internal retry flows or dedupe internal retry spans in the runtime (Engineering task; priority P0).
- Cost/trace playbook: formalize a checklist for span-count vs cost correlation and add to the runbook (Owner: Maya).
- Dashboardization: build a standard correlation card component (Owner: Priya) to re-use across other routes.

Appendix — quick artifact references:
- Trace sampler query used for the sample set: "service:streaming-proxy and trace.duration < 2000ms and tags:RP-204" (saved in observability/queries/samples/retry-impact-2026-12-16)
- Repro script: telemetry-config/testbeds/repro/retry-loop.sh
- Jira: OBS-5472 (billing correlation), OBS-5473 (proxy revert canary), OBS-5474 (KV-handle propagation task)

Notes to self / informal:
- Could be a good case study for the span-economics doc — show how a small control-flow change cascaded into cost.
- Keep this note as the canonical weeknote for this investigation; will extract a short executive one-pager if Finance asks.

Next sync: brief standup on 2026-12-17 09:30 PT for canary check; full deep-dive scheduled 2026-12-18 10:00 PT with Claire and runtime leads.
